_comment: Shared contract for the roster-aware 'who should I pick now' rule.
The rule lives twice on purpose: src/mockDraft.py::best_available drives the
backtest, and frontend/src/lib/bestAvailable.ts drives the live board (the
board must keep working with no Python process running on draft day). Two
implementations of the same math is exactly how liveDraft.ts and keeper.py
already drifted apart with only a comment holding them together.
Both are run against this file. A change to either that is not a change to
`rules` pins the league constants themselves: Python asserts they still equal
fallback constants match. So a slot change in Python cannot silently leave

cases.name: takes the highest vorp when nothing constrains the pick
skips a player already off the board
skips a position already at its cap
cases.why: Four centers is the cap; a fifth can never leave the bench.

cases.name: a keeper at a position counts against that position's cap
cases.why: Kept goalie plus one drafted fills both G slots; a third can never start.

cases.name: without a keeper list the base cap applies unchanged
cases.why: The opponent path passes no keepers and must not inherit your constraints.

cases.name: reserves the last picks for unfilled starting slots
cases.why: One pick left and one empty G slot: the 99-VORP center cannot be started.

cases.name: reserves when needs outnumber the picks left, not only when equal
cases.why: Two G slots open and one pick: still forced, and the >= is what does it.

cases.name: a keeper fills a starting slot and lifts the reservation
cases.why: Kept goalie means G is not a need, so the best player is free to win.

cases.name: falls back to best available when the needed position is empty
cases.why: A skipped pick would hand the comparison away for free.

cases.name: picks_left null disables the reservation rule entirely
cases.why: Opponent substitutions are unmodelled; inventing needs for them would skew the result.

cases.name: plenty of picks left leaves the early board undistorted
cases.why: Reserving only the tail is the point: needs can still be met later.

cases.name: an empty board yields no pick
a fully taken board yields no pick
